failures.title: Ford T7DB Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Injector Seal Failure ("Black Death") - 2008-2015
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to escape into the valve cover. This creates a hard, black, tarry carbon buildup around the injector base, which can eventually lead to compression loss or damage to the injector itself.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the injector seals is a relatively inexpensive fix. However, if ignored, the resulting damage to the cylinder head or injectors often necessitates a full T7DB engine replacement.

items.title: DPF Clogging and EGR Valve Issues - Urban Driving
items.whatHappens: The T7DB relies on a Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) and Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) system to meet emissions standards. Frequent short, urban journeys prevent the DPF from reaching the temperatures required for active regeneration, leading to restrictive soot buildup and subsequent limp mode.
items.repairVsReplace: A forced regeneration or EGR clean can resolve early symptoms. However, chronic neglect can cause excessive backpressure, leading to turbocharger failure and making a reconditioned T7DB the most reliable long-term solution.

failures.goodYearsLine: The T7DB is generally considered one of the more robust iterations of the Duratorq family, particularly when compared to the earlier 1.8 TDCi units. Regular oil changes using Ford-approved 5W-30 low-SAPS oil significantly extend the life of both the DPF and the timing components .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the T7DB
variants.intro: The T7DB is a specific engine code within Ford’s broader 2.0-litre Duratorq TDCi family. While it shares its core architecture with several similar codes, confirming your exact designation is critical because ECU mapping, turbocharger plumbing, and mounting points can differ between revisions. The T7DB is most commonly confused with: - T7DA: A closely related 2.0 TDCi variant, often found in similar Focus and Mondeo models but with different power tuning or emissions hardware . - T8DA: Another 2.0 TDCi code, typically featuring different turbocharger specifications or Euro 5 calibration updates .

relatives.description: The direct successor introduced in 2016, featuring a revised timing setup but bringing its own documented wet belt concerns in later models.
A larger displacement variant of the Duratorq family often found in heavier Mondeo and Transit applications, sharing similar injector and DPF maintenance requirements.
The T7DB shares its core architecture with the Peugeot/Citroën DW10 family, meaning many internal components and failure patterns (like injector seal wear) are identical across both brands.

variants.closing: Fitting the wrong revision can result in ECU communication errors, mismatched turbo boost levels, or physical mounting conflicts. The engine code is stamped directly on the engine block, typically on a machined pad near the oil filter housing or on the vehicle’s VIN plate under the bonnet. It is also listed on your V5C logbook. buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement T7DB - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used T7DB can be a budget-friendly option for older Mondeo or Focus models, but it carries inherent risks. Given the prevalence of DPF and injector seal issues in this family, a used unit should only be purchased if it comes with verifiable service history proving recent EGR/DPF maintenance and injector health.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended path for a T7DB replacement. A proper reconditioning process will address the engine's known weak points by fitting new injector seals, thoroughly cleaning or replacing the EGR valve, and ensuring the DPF is fully functional, providing a reliable, long-term fix.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage Kuga or Mondeo examples where the cylinder bores or crankshaft bearings have suffered wear. A comprehensive rebuild should include new pistons, rings, and a refreshed turbocharger to restore the T7DB to better-than-factory reliability.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network provides nationwide supply and fit options, ensuring your replacement T7DB is installed by Ford specialists with a minimum 12-month warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Host vehicles like the Ford Focus Mk3 and Mondeo Mk4 typically retain values between £2,500 and £8,000 depending on condition and mileage . With reconditioned T7DB units starting from £1,200, replacement represents a financially viable investment for well-maintained examples, though owners of sub-£3,000 vehicles should carefully evaluate scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a major repair.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the Ford T7DB 2.0 TDCi?
items.answer: The most common failures on the Ford T7DB are injector seal wear ("Black Death") and DPF clogging, typically occurring between 80,000 and 120,000 miles. Degraded injector seals allow combustion gases to escape, causing carbon buildup, while frequent short journeys prevent DPF regeneration, leading to restrictive soot buildup and limp mode.

Frequent short journeys prevent DPF regeneration, leading to restrictive soot buildup and limp mode.

items.question: Which Ford models use the T7DB engine?
items.answer: The T7DB engine code is fitted to the Ford Focus Mk3, Ford Mondeo Mk4, and Ford Kuga Mk1 and Mk2. It served as the primary 2.0-litre diesel workhorse for these models between 2008 and 2015, with power outputs typically ranging from 115hp to 163hp depending on the specific vehicle tune.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned T7DB engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned T7DB is the most recommended path, as a proper reconditioning process will fit new injector seals and ensure the DPF and EGR systems are fully functional. Used engines are only viable if they have verifiable service history proving recent EGR/DPF maintenance, otherwise you risk inheriting hidden oil starvation or turbo damage.

items.answer: The T7DB engine code is stamped directly on the engine block, typically on a machined pad near the oil filter housing or on the vehicle’s VIN plate under the bonnet. It is also listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or via a VIN decoder, and is commonly confused with the T7DA or T8DA, which have different ECU mapping and turbo specifications.
